name: Cryptographic Protocol Analysis
description: Covers analysis of cryptographic protocol designs and specifications for their intended security properties (authentication, key secrecy, forward secrecy, replay and downgrade resistance). Includes established protocols such as SSH, IPsec/IKE and secure messaging protocols, custom and proprietary protocols, and the use of formal verification tools such as Tamarin and ProVerif to model and verify protocol properties. TLS assessment specifically belongs to CRYPTO-PKI-TLS. Assessment of deployed end-to-end encrypted messaging systems belongs to CRYPTO-PROTO-E2EE.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to cryptographic protocol analysis

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands protocol security goals and common protocol failure classes
evidence: Can explain authentication, key secrecy, forward secrecy and key compromise impersonation as protocol properties
Aware of classic protocol attacks (replay, reflection, man-in-the-middle, downgrade, unknown key share)
Understands the Dolev-Yao attacker model at a conceptual level

2.label: Guided Practice
evidence: Draws message sequence diagrams for an established protocol from its specification
Identifies the claimed security properties and the assumptions they rely on with guidance
Reviews protocol configuration (algorithms, versions, authentication modes) for SSH or IPsec deployments
Documents analysis in the lab's reporting template

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently analyses established and custom protocols
evidence: Evaluates custom or proprietary protocols against their claimed security properties and identifies design flaws
Builds and runs a formal model of a protocol in Tamarin or ProVerif and interprets the results
Assesses downgrade, negotiation and state machine weaknesses in protocol implementations
Produces findings that clearly separate design flaws, specification ambiguities and implementation defects

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Analyses complex protocols; reviews analyses; mentors team
evidence: Models complex protocols (group messaging, multi-stage key exchange) and their compromise scenarios
Assesses the gap between formal models and real implementations and the resulting residual risk
Technically reviews protocol analysis reports and formal models
Mentors analysts on protocol analysis and formal verification

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognised authority on cryptographic protocols; defines methodology; publishes research
evidence: Defines the lab's protocol analysis methodology including when formal verification is required
Publishes research on protocol attacks or verification
Contributes to protocol standardisation (e.g. IETF working groups)
Advises vendors on secure protocol design

assessment_methods.description: Given the specification of a custom key-exchange protocol with a seeded design flaw, identify the flaw, demonstrate it with a Tamarin or ProVerif model, and propose a corrected design
Review a protocol analysis report for correct statement of security properties and attacker model, soundness of the analysis and clear separation of design and implementation findings
